sentences.cn_text: 20世纪70年代汤姆·斯韦特纳姆加入美国林务局时，他的任务是「扑灭一切火情」，他回忆道。
sentences.en_text: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to “put everything out,” he recalled.

sentences.cn_text: 但当斯韦特纳姆在亚利桑那大学树轮研究实验室攻读研究生时，他惊讶地发现，在欧洲殖民者抵达美洲大陆之前的数百年间，曾发生过反复多次的火灾，均有记录在案。
sentences.en_text: But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona’s Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent.

sentences.cn_text: 他分析的一些树木，其年轮上有超过20处火灾疤痕。
sentences.en_text: Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings.

sentences.cn_text: 火灾如此频繁发生这一事实意味着它们不可能严重到足以杀死大部分树木。
sentences.en_text: The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn’t have been severe enough to kill most trees.

sentences.cn_text: 相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁发生的低烈度火灾使许多生态系统更加健康。
sentences.en_text: Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier.

sentences.cn_text: 它们清除森林中的枯木和病树，减少了竞争并遏制了疾病传播。
sentences.en_text: They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease.

sentences.cn_text: 由于可燃物质无法在地表堆积，火势往往缓慢推进，并在抵达先前燃烧过的区域时自行熄灭。
sentences.en_text: Because flammable material couldn’t build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move Slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns.

sentences.cn_text: 2022年，斯韦特纳姆与其他科学家合作，编制了一个覆盖全美洲大陆的火灾疤痕树数据库。
sentences.en_text: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent.

sentences.cn_text: 他们的北美树轮火疤网络（NAFSN）为上个月发表的一项研究提供了基础。
sentences.en_text: Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month.

sentences.cn_text: 在该研究中，研究人员将历史火灾频率与过去几十年记录的野火进行对比，发现了一个显著的缺口。
sentences.en_text: In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall.

sentences.cn_text: NAFSN站点经历的火灾次数不到在没有火灾扑灭措施情况下预期次数的四分之一。
sentences.en_text: The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression.

sentences.cn_text: 国际野火协会前主席凯利·马丁说，这一缺口证明了现代消防的有效性。
sentences.en_text: This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire.

sentences.cn_text: 「然而，火灾扑灭与气候变化的综合后果已削弱了人类扑灭火灾的能力，尤其是那些在最危险天气条件下引发的火灾。」
sentences.en_text: “Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity’s ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions.”

sentences.cn_text: 马丁说，为了防止整个生态系统化为乌有，人们必须将有益的火带回需要它的地方。
sentences.en_text: To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it.

sentences.cn_text: 在优胜美地国家公园，马丁监督使用所谓的计划性燃烧来增强地貌的韧性。
sentences.en_text: At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient.

sentences.cn_text: 这些火灾经过周密规划，在天气条件便于控制火势的时期有意点燃，有助于清除公园重要设施周围积累的部分可燃物。
sentences.en_text: These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park’s facilities.

sentences.cn_text: 研究表明，这些计划性燃烧能降低后续野火的烈度，即使后来的火灾发生在最危险的天气条件下。
sentences.en_text: Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions.

sentences.cn_text: 专家表示，尽管科学家和政府官员日益认同森林需要更多火灾，但气候变化正使这一策略变得更具挑战性。
sentences.en_text: Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said.

sentences.cn_text: 「这是一把双刃剑，因为在气候变化下野火变得更加严重、规模更大，我们更加需要这项工作，但与此同时这项工作也变得更具挑战性，」华盛顿大学火灾生态学家苏珊·普里查德说道。
sentences.en_text: “It’s a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging,” said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.
